definition_en: to harm someone's character with too much kindness, or to ruin something
core_image: 被惯坏的孩子把玩具扔了一地
scene: 祖父母把孙子宠坏了。The grandparents spoil their grandson.
sceneCN: 这里 spoil 是「宠坏、溺爱」（第 1 个义项）；句意：祖父母把孙子宠坏了。

senses.title: Ruin with kindness
senses.definition: to harm someone's character by giving too much
senses.definitionCN: 因给予过多而损害某人的性格
senses.example: The grandparents spoil their grandson.
senses.exampleCN: 祖父母把孙子宠坏了。
senses.why: This sense is central in family talk.
senses.whyCN: 这是家庭语境中最核心的用法。

senses.title: Ruin an event
senses.definition: to damage or ruin something
senses.definitionCN: 损坏或毁掉某事
senses.example: The rain spoiled our picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 这场雨毁了我们的野餐。
senses.why: The older sense is direct damage.
senses.whyCN: 较古老的义项是直接的损坏。

senses.title: Go bad
senses.definition: to become bad or unfit to eat
senses.definitionCN: 变坏、不再适合食用
senses.example: The fruit will spoil in the heat.
senses.exampleCN: 水果在高温下会变质。
senses.why: Food damage happens without anyone acting.
senses.whyCN: 食物变坏是无人动手也会发生的事。

intro.en: Spoil comes from Latin spoliare, to strip or plunder.
intro.cn: spoil 来自拉丁语 spoliare，意为剥夺、掠夺。

items.en: Spoliare meant to strip or rob.
items.cn: spoliare 意为剥夺、抢劫。

items.en: Espoillier meant to plunder.
items.cn: espoillier 意为掠夺。

items.en: Spoilen meant to rob or damage.
items.cn: spoil 在中古英语中意为抢劫、损坏。

items.en: The sense softened to harming character.
items.cn: 词义柔化为损害性格。

items.en: Food spoiling meant going bad.
items.cn: 食物 spoil 表示变质。

note.en: Spoil is compared with look-alike words and words for ruining.
note.cn: 把 spoil 与形近词以及表示毁坏的词作比较。

entries.definition: to treat with too much care

normalIntro.en: Spoil once meant to plunder; now it means to damage with too much.

normal.en: He spoiled the ending for me.

abstract.en: What is never refused is never valued.

abstract.en: Fruit and favor both turn with time.
abstract.cn: 水果与恩宠，都会随时间变味。

examples.en: The grandparents spoil their grandson.

examples.en: The rain spoiled our picnic.

examples.en: The fruit will spoil in the heat.

core.en: Damage done by taking or giving too much.
core.cn: 取之过多或给之过多造成的损坏。

branches.cn: 孩子扔了玩具还在笑。

branches.en: Rain falls on a laid table.
branches.cn: 雨落在摆好的餐桌上。

branches.en: Fruit softens in a warm bowl.
branches.cn: 水果在温热的碗里变软。

branches.en: Too much care and too much rain both ruin.
branches.cn: 过多的照顾与过多的雨，都会毁掉。

branches.cn: 被损坏的，也会继续腐坏。

intro.en: Spoil forms verb parts, adjectives, and nouns.
intro.cn: spoil 构成动词变化、形容词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is spoliare, to strip.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 spoliare，意为剥夺。

items.meaning: one who spoils, or a plot leak

definition_en: a man who speaks for a group
core_image: 一位代表站在麦克风前回答提问
scene: 公司发言人否认了这一说法。The company spokesman denied the claim.
sceneCN: 这里 spokesman 是「发言人」（第 1 个义项）；句意：公司发言人否认了这一说法。

senses.title: Speaker for an organization
senses.definition: a man who speaks officially for an organization
senses.definitionCN: 代表机构正式发言的男性
senses.example: The company spokesman denied the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 公司发言人否认了这一说法。
senses.why: The official role is the main modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 官方职务是现代最主要的义项。

senses.title: Voice of a group
senses.definition: a person who expresses the views of a group
senses.definitionCN: 表达某个群体观点的人
senses.example: He became the spokesman for the farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 他成了农民的代言人。
senses.why: The role extends beyond formal organizations.
senses.whyCN: 这个角色不限于正式机构。

senses.title: Official speaker role
senses.definition: the role itself, in older generic use
senses.definitionCN: 旧时不分性别的泛指用法

senses.exampleCN: 该团体的发言人宣读了声明。

note.en: Spokesman is compared with look-alike words and words for representatives.

a person sent to speak for a group

abstract.en: A spokesman lends one voice to many.

abstract.en: The words are his; the view is theirs.

abstract.en: Every group needs a mouth.

examples.en: The company spokesman denied the claim.

sensesIntro.en: Spokesman means an official speaker for an organization, a group's voice, or the role itself.
sensesIntro.cn: spokesman 指机构的正式发言人、群体的代言人，或发言人这一职务。

core.en: One mouth speaking for many.
core.cn: 一张替许多人说话的嘴。

branches.en: Microphones wait on a bare table.
branches.cn: 麦克风在空桌上等待。

branches.en: A farmer stands before a crowd.
branches.cn: 一位农民站在人群前。

branches.en: A printed statement is read aloud.
branches.cn: 一份印好的声明被大声读出。

branches.en: A formal role grows from a shared voice.
branches.cn: 正式职务源自共同的声音。

branches.en: The crowd's view becomes one sentence.
branches.cn: 众人的观点凝成一句话。

intro.en: Spokesman forms plurals and gender-neutral variants.

latinIntro.en: Spokesman has no Latin root; speak is Germanic.

a neutral word for a speaker

definition_en: a person or company that pays for an event or supports someone
core_image: 一块印着品牌名的赛事背景板
scene: 这家银行是比赛的赞助商。The bank is a sponsor of the race.
sceneCN: 这里 sponsor 是「赞助商」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这家银行是比赛的赞助商。

senses.title: A financial backer
senses.definition: a person or company that pays for an event
senses.definitionCN: 为活动出资的个人或公司
senses.example: The bank is a sponsor of the race.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行是比赛的赞助商。
senses.why: Commercial backing is the most common sense.
senses.whyCN: 商业赞助是最常见的义项。

senses.title: One who proposes
senses.definition: a person who proposes or supports a plan or law
senses.definitionCN: 提出或支持计划、法律的人
senses.example: She was the sponsor of the new law.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这项新法律的发起人。
senses.why: Support begins with a formal proposal.
senses.whyCN: 支持始于正式的提议。

senses.title: To fund an event
senses.definition: to pay for or support an event or person
senses.definitionCN: 为活动或某人出资支持
senses.example: A local firm sponsors the team.

senses.why: The noun became a verb of support.

sensesIntro.en: Sponsor means a financial backer, a proposer of a plan, or to fund an event.

senses.title: The eating tool

intro.en: Spur is an old riding word of Germanic origin.
intro.cn: spur 是源自古英语的骑术词，属日耳曼语。

items.en: Spura named a spiked tool on a rider's heel.
items.cn: spura 指骑手靴跟上的带刺工具。

items.en: Spori carried the same sense into northern English.
items.cn: spori 把相同的含义带进英格兰北部。

items.en: Spur kept the tool and grew a figurative sense.
items.cn: spur 保留工具义，并发展出比喻义。

items.en: It meant anything that urges action.
items.cn: 它指任何促使人行动的事物。

items.en: Spur on became a common phrase.
items.cn: spur on 成为常见短语。

note.en: Spur is compared with look-alike words and words for encouragement.
note.cn: 把 spur 与形近词以及表示激励的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Spur is a small spike that makes a big animal move.
normalIntro.cn: spur 是一根让小刺推动庞然大物的小尖刺。

normal.en: The news spurred us to act.
He bought it on the spur of the moment.

normal.cn: 降低税收可能促进增长。

abstract.en: A spur is a question that will not wait.
abstract.cn: 马刺，是一个不肯等的问题。

abstract.en: Small spikes move large bodies.
abstract.cn: 小小的尖刺，推动庞大的身体。

abstract.en: What urges you forward also leaves a mark.
abstract.cn: 催你向前的，也会留下痕迹。

examples.en: The prize was a spur to work harder.
examples.cn: 这份奖品是更努力工作的刺激。

examples.en: The rider touched the horse with his spurs.
examples.cn: 骑手用马刺轻碰马身。

examples.en: Curiosity spurred her to keep learning.
examples.cn: 好奇心促使她继续学习。

dict_mnemonic.text: spur 是「马刺」，引申为「刺激、激励」；spur on 是激励，spur growth 是促进增长，spur of the moment 是一时冲动；过去式是 spurred。

root: 来自古英语 spura（马刺），与古诺尔斯语 spori 同源，核心义为靴跟上的尖刺，后引申为任何促人行动的刺激。

sensesIntro.en: Spur means a stimulus, a rider's spiked tool, or to urge someone forward.
sensesIntro.cn: spur 指刺激、马刺，或激励某人向前。

core.en: A small point that starts a large motion.
core.cn: 启动巨大运动的一个小尖点。

branches.en: A prize waits on a shelf.
branches.cn: 奖品摆在架子上。

branches.en: Metal shines at a rider's heel.
branches.cn: 金属在骑手靴跟闪光。

branches.en: A question sends a student back to books.
branches.cn: 一个问题把学生送回书本。

branches.en: The tool and the motive are one image.
branches.cn: 工具与动机，是同一个意象。

branches.en: A touch becomes a command to move.
branches.cn: 轻轻一碰，变成前进的命令。

intro.en: Spur forms verb parts and a few compounds.
intro.cn: spur 构成动词变化和少量复合词。

latinIntro.en: Spur has no Latin root; it is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: spur 没有拉丁词根，它属日耳曼语。

items.example: The coach kept spurring the team.

items.exampleCN: 年轻的骑手没有戴马刺。

items.example: The machine uses a spur gear.
A spur track leads to the mill.

definition_en: a small group of people working or playing together
core_image: 几名士兵排成一小队在清晨出发
scene: 一支小队在清晨出发。A squad set out at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 squad 是「小队」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一支小队在清晨出发。

senses.title: Small military unit
senses.definition: a small group of soldiers or police officers
senses.definitionCN: 一小队士兵或警察
senses.example: A squad set out at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 一支小队在清晨出发。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老也最具体的义项。

senses.title: Sports group
senses.definition: a group of players chosen to compete
senses.definitionCN: 被选去参赛的一组运动员
senses.example: The coach named the squad for the match.
senses.exampleCN: 教练公布了参赛的运动队名单。
senses.why: The unit idea moved from army to sport.
senses.whyCN: 「小队」的概念从军队延伸到体育。

senses.title: Work crew
senses.definition: a small team doing a particular job
senses.definitionCN: 执行特定任务的小组
senses.example: A squad of workers repaired the road.
senses.exampleCN: 一队工人修好了这条路。
senses.why: Any small task group can be called a squad.
senses.whyCN: 任何小型任务小组都可称为 squad。

intro.en: Squad comes from Italian squadra, a square or a troop, from Latin exquadrare.
intro.cn: squad 来自意大利语 squadra（方形、队伍），其源头是拉丁语 exquadrare。

items.en: Exquadrare meant to make square.

items.en: Squadra meant a square or a troop.
items.cn: squadra 意为方形或队伍。

items.en: Escouade meant a small troop.

items.en: Squad entered as a small military unit.
items.cn: squad 以小型军事单位的意义进入英语。

items.en: The sports sense grew in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 体育义项在二十世纪发展起来。

note.en: Squad is compared with look-alike words and words for groups.

a single part of a larger group
a group working on a ship or job

normalIntro.en: Squad began as a square-shaped troop and now means any small team.
normalIntro.cn: squad 原指排成方阵的队伍，如今泛指任何小型团队。

normal.en: He leads a road repair squad.

abstract.en: A square of people becomes a squad.
abstract.cn: 站成方形的一群人，就成为一支小队。

abstract.en: Small groups move faster than crowds.
abstract.cn: 小队比人群行动得更快。

abstract.en: Order turns many hands into one unit.
abstract.cn: 秩序把许多只手合成一个整体。

examples.en: A squad set out at dawn.

examples.en: A squad of workers repaired the road.
examples.cn: 一队工人修好了这条路。

dict_mnemonic.text: squad 是「小队、运动队」；squad car 是警车，squad leader 是小队长；复数直接加 s 变 squads。

root: 来自意大利语 squadra（方形、队伍），源头是拉丁语 exquadrare（使成方形）；队伍排成方阵，因而引申出「小队、班」。

sensesIntro.en: Squad means a small military unit, a sports group, or a work crew.
sensesIntro.cn: squad 指小型军事单位、运动队或工作班组。

core.en: A small ordered group acting as one.
core.cn: 作为一个整体行动的小型有序队伍。

branches.en: Soldiers march in a tight line.
branches.cn: 士兵排成紧密的一列行进。

branches.en: Players gather around their coach.
branches.cn: 运动员围在教练身边。

branches.en: Workers lift tools from a truck.
branches.cn: 工人从卡车上搬下工具。

branches.en: Both army and sport need a chosen few.
branches.cn: 军队与体育都需要挑选出的一小群人。

branches.en: Team and crew both work as one body.
branches.cn: 运动队与班组都作为一个整体运作。

intro.en: Squad forms plurals and a few related nouns.
intro.cn: squad 构成复数以及若干相关名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is exquadrare, to make square.

items.example: A squad set out at dawn.
Two squads met at the gate.

definition_zh: 正方形；广场；平方；公正的
definition_en: a shape with four equal sides, an open city space, or fair and honest
core_image: 广场地砖拼成整齐的正方形
scene: 孩子们在广场上放风筝。The children flew kites in the square.
sceneCN: 这里 square 是「广场」（第 2 个义项）；句意：孩子们在广场上放风筝。

senses.title: Four-sided shape
senses.definition: a shape with four equal sides and four right angles
senses.definitionCN: 四条边相等、四个角都是直角的图形
senses.example: She drew a square on the board.
senses.exampleCN: 她在黑板上画了一个正方形。
senses.why: This is the concrete shape sense.

senses.title: Open city space
senses.definition: an open area in a town, often with buildings around it
senses.definitionCN: 城镇中四周常有建筑的开阔场地
senses.example: The children flew kites in the square.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在广场上放风筝。
senses.why: The shape became a place in old towns.
senses.whyCN: 在古老城镇里，方形的地块变成了场所。

senses.title: Product of a number

senses.definitionCN: 一个数自乘所得的结果

senses.why: A square number is drawn as a square array.

senses.title: Fair and honest

senses.definitionCN: 待人处事诚实公平的

intro.en: Square comes from Latin exquadrare, to make square, through Old French esquarre.

items.en: Exquadrare meant to make square.

items.cn: esquarre 意为方形或曲尺。

note.en: Square is compared with look-alike words and words for open places.

normal.en: Fold the paper into a square.

The room is twelve square metres.

abstract.en: Equal sides make a steady shape.

abstract.en: Every number can grow into a square.

sensesIntro.en: Square names a shape, a town space, a product of multiplication, or fair conduct.

core.en: Four equal sides meeting at right angles.

definition_en: to press something firmly, to get liquid out, or to force your way into a small space
core_image: 双手把柠檬挤出一滴汁
scene: 她挤了一点柠檬汁。She squeezed a little lemon juice.
sceneCN: 这里 squeeze 是「挤压、榨取」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她挤了一点柠檬汁。

senses.title: Press firmly
senses.definition: to press something hard from both sides
senses.definitionCN: 从两边用力压某物
senses.example: She squeezed the lemon gently.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻轻挤压柠檬。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的物理义项。

senses.title: Force out
senses.definition: to get liquid or money out by pressure
senses.definitionCN: 靠压力取得液体或钱财

senses.exampleCN: 他们从预算里又榨出一些钱。
senses.why: Pressure applied to people yields money too.
senses.whyCN: 对人施压也能得到钱财。

senses.title: Crowd in
senses.definition: to force yourself into a narrow space
senses.definitionCN: 勉强进入狭窄空间
senses.example: We squeezed into the last seats.
senses.exampleCN: 我们挤进了最后几个座位。
senses.why: A body under pressure fits a small space.
senses.whyCN: 身体受压就能塞进狭小空间。

intro.cn: squeeze 来自古英语 cwysan（压），更深来源不确定。

normal.en: Squeeze the lemon into the tea.

normal.cn: 他紧紧握了一下我的手。

normal.en: We squeezed into a tiny car.

abstract.en: Pressure brings out what is inside.
abstract.cn: 压力能逼出里面的东西。

abstract.en: A narrow door still lets people through.
abstract.cn: 窄门仍能让人通过。

abstract.en: Too much squeezing leaves a dry fruit.

examples.en: She squeezed the lemon gently.

branches.cn: 肩膀从人群中挤过去。

branches.cn: 压水果与压人，都会有所得。

intro.en: Squeeze forms verb parts, an agent noun, and adjectives.

senses.title: Firmly fixed
senses.definition: strongly built and not likely to move

senses.why: The physical sense supports the abstract one.

senses.title: Building for horses

intro.en: Stable forms comparisons, plurals, and a family of steady words.

definition_en: a neat pile of things, to put things in a pile, or the shelves in a library

scene: 桌上堆着一摞书。A stack of books lay on the table.

senses.title: Neat pile

senses.definitionCN: 一件件叠放整齐的一堆东西

senses.title: Put in a pile

senses.title: Library shelves

examples.en: She found the book in the stacks.

dict_mnemonic.text: stack 是「一摞、堆叠」；a stack of books 是一摞书，stack up 是堆积，chimney stack 是烟囱；图书馆的 stacks 指书库。

sensesIntro.en: Stack means a neat pile, the act of piling, or library shelves.

core.en: Things laid one on top of another.

definition_zh: 体育场；古希腊赛跑场；斯塔德（长度单位）
definition_en: a large sports ground with seats around it, or the ancient Greek racecourse
core_image: 人群涌进环形的体育场看台
scene: 人群涌进体育场。The crowd poured into the stadium.

pos.zh: 斯塔德（古希腊长度单位）

senses.title: Sports ground
senses.definition: a large ground for sports with rows of seats around it
senses.definitionCN: 四周设有成排座位的巨大运动场地
senses.example: The crowd poured into the stadium.
senses.exampleCN: 人群涌进体育场。
senses.why: This is the everyday modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最常见的义项。

senses.title: Greek racecourse
senses.definition: the ancient Greek track used for foot races
senses.definitionCN: 古希腊用于赛跑的跑道
senses.example: Runners raced in the ancient stadium.
senses.exampleCN: 赛跑者在古老的赛跑场上竞速。
senses.why: The word began as the name of this track.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初就是这条跑道的名称。

senses.title: Greek length unit
senses.definition: an ancient Greek unit of length, about one hundred and eighty-five metres
senses.definitionCN: 古希腊长度单位，约合一百八十五米
senses.example: The track was one stadium long.
senses.exampleCN: 这条跑道长一个斯塔德。

intro.en: Stadium comes from Greek stadion, a racecourse and a unit of length, through Latin stadium.

items.en: Stadion meant a racecourse and its length.

items.en: The Greek length sense survives in history books.

note.en: Stadium is compared with look-alike words and words for sports grounds.
note.cn: 把 stadium 与形近词以及表示运动场地的词作比较。

sensesIntro.en: Stadium means a modern sports ground, the ancient Greek racecourse, or a Greek length unit.
sensesIntro.cn: stadium 指现代体育场、古希腊赛跑场，或古希腊长度单位。

branches.en: Thousands fill the curved seats.

definition_en: the people who work for an organization, a strong stick, or the five lines of written music
core_image: 职员们拿着文件走过办公室走廊
scene: 全体员工参加了会议。The whole staff attended the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 staff 是「全体职员」（第 1 个义项）；句意：全体员工参加了会议。

senses.title: Employees
senses.definition: all the people who work for an organization
senses.definitionCN: 为一个机构工作的所有人
senses.example: The whole staff attended the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 全体员工参加了会议。
senses.why: This is the dominant modern sense.

senses.definitionCN: 用于支撑身体的长而结实的棍子

items.exampleCN: 他的声音听起来很做作。
一名舞台工作人员搬动了椅子。

definition_en: a dirty mark, to colour something, or to damage a reputation
core_image: 桌布上一块深色的墨水渍
scene: 墨水在桌布上留下污渍。The ink left a stain on the cloth.
sceneCN: 这里 stain 是「污渍」（第 1 个义项）；句意：墨水在桌布上留下污渍。

senses.title: Dirty mark
senses.definition: a dirty mark that is hard to remove
senses.definitionCN: 难以去除的脏痕
senses.example: The ink left a stain on the cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 墨水在桌布上留下污渍。
senses.why: This is the everyday physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常最常用的具体义项。

senses.title: Colour wood or cloth
senses.definition: to give colour to wood or fabric
senses.definitionCN: 给木材或织物上色
senses.example: They stained the wood dark brown.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把木头染成深棕色。
senses.why: A stain can be wanted, not just dirt.
senses.whyCN: 染色可以是有意为之，而不只是脏污。

senses.title: Damage a name
senses.definition: to damage someone's reputation
senses.definitionCN: 损害某人的名声
senses.example: The scandal stained his name.
senses.exampleCN: 这桩丑闻玷污了他的名声。
senses.why: A mark on cloth became a mark on character.
senses.whyCN: 布上的印记变成了人格上的污点。

intro.en: Stain comes from Old French desteindre, to take colour away, from Latin tingere, to dye.
intro.cn: stain 来自古法语 desteindre（使褪色），源头是拉丁语 tingere（染色）。

items.en: Tingere meant to dye or wet.
items.cn: tingere 意为染色或浸湿。

items.en: Desteindre meant to take colour away.
items.cn: desteindre 意为使褪色。

items.en: Stain meant to discolour or spot.
items.cn: stain 意为使变色、留下斑点。

items.en: The noun named the mark itself.
items.cn: 名词义指印记本身。

items.en: The moral sense grew from visible marks.
items.cn: 道德义由可见的印记引申而来。

note.en: Stain is compared with look-alike words and words for marks.
note.cn: 把 stain 与形近词以及表示印记的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Stain is a mark left behind, whether on cloth, wood, or a name.
normalIntro.cn: stain 是留下的印记，无论在布上、木上，还是在名声上。

normal.en: There is a stain on your shirt.

abstract.en: Some marks wash out; some do not.
abstract.cn: 有些印记洗得掉，有些洗不掉。

abstract.en: Colour and dirt share one word.
abstract.cn: 色彩与污垢，共用一个词。

abstract.en: A name, once stained, keeps the shape of the mark.
abstract.cn: 名声一旦被玷污，就留下印记的形状。

examples.en: The ink left a stain on the cloth.
examples.cn: 墨水在桌布上留下污渍。

examples.en: They stained the wood dark brown.
examples.cn: 他们把木头染成深棕色。

examples.en: The scandal stained his name.
examples.cn: 这桩丑闻玷污了他的名声。

dict_mnemonic.text: stain 是「污渍」，也指「染色、玷污」；coffee stain 是咖啡渍，stain remover 是去污剂，stained glass 是彩色玻璃；stainless 是不锈的。

root: 来自古法语 desteindre（使褪色），源头是拉丁语 tingere（染色）；由「使布变色」引申为污渍、有意染色，再引申为玷污名声。

sensesIntro.en: Stain means a dirty mark, the act of colouring, or damage to a reputation.
sensesIntro.cn: stain 指污渍、染色，或对名声的玷污。

core.en: A colour mark left on a surface.
core.cn: 留在表面上的颜色印记。

branches.en: Ink spreads into a dark patch.
branches.cn: 墨水晕开成一块深色印记。

branches.en: A brush lays colour on wood.
branches.cn: 刷子把颜色涂在木头上。

branches.en: Whispers leave a shadow on a name.
branches.cn: 流言在名声上留下阴影。

branches.en: The same mark may be dirt or design.
branches.cn: 同一个印记，可能是污垢，也可能是设计。

branches.en: Cloth and character both keep a mark.
branches.cn: 布匹与人格，都会留下印记。

intro.en: Stain forms verb parts and a family of colour words.
intro.cn: stain 构成动词变化以及一组与颜色相关的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is tingere, to dye.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁语源头是 tingere，意为染色。

items.example: The stain will not come out.
There are stains on the rug.
Staining the table takes a day.

items.exampleCN: 两名染色工在那里干活。

definition_en: a set of steps inside a building, or one single step
core_image: 老宅里一段木制楼梯向上延伸
scene: 她慢慢走上楼梯。She walked slowly up the stairs.
sceneCN: 这里 stair 是「楼梯」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她慢慢走上楼梯。

senses.title: Flight of steps
senses.definition: a set of steps that leads from one floor to another
senses.definitionCN: 连接上下楼层的一组台阶
senses.example: She walked slowly up the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她慢慢走上楼梯。
senses.why: The plural form is the usual word for the whole flight.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式通常指整段楼梯。

senses.title: Single step
senses.definition: one step in a set of stairs
senses.definitionCN: 一组楼梯中的一级台阶
senses.example: He sat on the bottom stair.
senses.exampleCN: 他坐在最下面一级台阶上。
senses.why: The singular names just one step.
senses.whyCN: 单数形式只指一级台阶。

intro.en: Stair comes from Old English stæger, a set of steps, from a Germanic root meaning to climb.
intro.cn: stair 来自古英语 stæger（一组台阶），源于意为「攀爬」的日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root meant to climb or rise.
items.cn: 该词根意为攀爬、上升。

items.en: Stæger meant a set of steps.
items.cn: stæger 意为一组台阶。

items.en: Stair named one step of a flight.
items.cn: stair 指一段楼梯中的一级。

items.en: The plural stairs became the usual name for a flight.
items.cn: 复数 stairs 成为整段楼梯的常用说法。

items.en: Compounds like staircase and stairway grew from it.
items.cn: staircase、stairway 等复合词由此产生。

note.en: Stair is compared with look-alike words and words for steps.
note.cn: 把 stair 与形近词以及表示台阶的词作比较。

entries.definition: a flat surface for the foot
a set of stairs and its frame
a frame with rungs for climbing

normalIntro.en: Stair is one step in the singular and the whole flight in the plural.
normalIntro.cn: stair 单数是一级台阶，复数则指整段楼梯。

normal.en: She sat on the bottom stair.
normal.cn: 她坐在最下面一级台阶上。

abstract.en: Every climb is made of single steps.
abstract.cn: 每一次攀登，都由一级级台阶组成。

abstract.en: One step is small; the flight is long.
abstract.cn: 一级很小，整段很长。

abstract.en: The way up is also the way home.
abstract.cn: 向上的路，也是回家的路。

examples.en: She walked slowly up the stairs.
examples.cn: 她慢慢走上楼梯。

examples.en: He sat on the bottom stair.
examples.cn: 他坐在最下面一级台阶上。

examples.en: The stairs are steep and narrow.
examples.cn: 这楼梯又陡又窄。

dict_mnemonic.text: stair 单数指「一级台阶」，复数 stairs 指「楼梯」；up the stairs 是上楼，a flight of stairs 是一段楼梯；staircase 是楼梯间。

root: 来自古英语 stæger（一组台阶），源于意为「攀爬、上升」的日耳曼语词根；单数指一级，复数指整段楼梯。

sensesIntro.en: Stair means a flight of steps or a single step.
sensesIntro.cn: stair 指一段楼梯或一级台阶。

core.en: A step that carries you upward.
core.cn: 把带向上方的一级台阶。

branches.en: A wooden flight turns at the landing.
branches.cn: 一段木楼梯在平台处转弯。

branches.en: One foot rests on the lowest step.
branches.cn: 一只脚踩在最下面一级。

branches.en: The whole stair reaches the upper room.
branches.cn: 整段楼梯通向上层房间。

branches.en: The single step is the unit of the climb.
branches.cn: 一级台阶是攀爬的基本单位。

branches.en: Many steps together make one stair.
branches.cn: 许多台阶合在一起，才成为一段楼梯。

intro.en: Stair forms plurals and compounds for parts of a building.
intro.cn: stair 构成复数以及表示建筑部件的复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: A stairway led to the roof.
